content: 1. Olin P, Hallander HO, Gustafsson L, Reizenstein E, Storsaeter J. This study discusses methodologies for interpreting immunogenicity data related to pertussis vaccines. Published in Clinical Infectious Diseases on December 15, 2001, Supplement 4, pages S288-S291. 2. Hadler SC, Francis DP, Maynard JE, Thompson SE, Judson FN, Echenberg DF, et al. This research evaluates the long-term immunogenicity and efficacy of the hepatitis B vaccine in homosexual men. Published in the New England Journal of Medicine on July 24, 1986, Volume 315, Issue 4, pages 209-214. 3. Szmuness W, Stevens CE, Harley EJ, Zang EA, Oleszko WR, William DC, et al. This clinical trial demonstrates the efficacy of the hepatitis B vaccine in a high-risk population in the United States. Published in the New England Journal of Medicine on October 9, 1980, Volume 303, Issue 15, pages 833-841. 4. Amanna IJ, Carlson NE, Slifka MK. This study examines the duration of humoral immunity to common viral and vaccine antigens. Published in the New England Journal of Medicine on November 8, 2007, Volume 357, Issue 19, pages 1903-1915. 5. Rothman KJ, Greenland S, Lash TL. The third edition of Modern Epidemiology provides a comprehensive overview of epidemiological methods and principles. Published by Lippincott Williams & Wilkins in Philadelphia, 2008. 6. Feavers I, Knezevic I, Powell M, Griffiths E. This report addresses challenges in evaluating and licensing new pneumococcal vaccines, based on a meeting held on July 7-8, 2008, in Ottawa, Canada. Published in Vaccine on June 8, 2009, Volume 27, Issue 28, pages 3681-3688. 7. Smith PG, Rodrigues LC, Fine PE. This paper discusses methods for assessing the protective efficacy of vaccines against common diseases using case-control and cohort studies. Published in the International Journal of Epidemiology in March 1984, Volume 13, Issue 1, pages 87-93. 8. Halloran ME, Haber M, Longini IM. This study explores the interpretation and estimation of vaccine efficacy in the presence of heterogeneity. Published in the American Journal of Epidemiology in 1992, Volume 136, Issue 3, pages 328-343. 9. Haber M, Watlet L, Halloran ME. This research examines the individual and population-level effectiveness of vaccination. Published in the International Journal of Epidemiology in 1995, Volume 24, Issue 6, pages 1249-1260. 10. White MT, Griffin JT, Drakeley CJ, Ghani AC. This study investigates the implications of heterogeneity in malaria exposure and vaccine response for interpreting vaccine efficacy trials. Published in Malaria Journal in 2010, Volume 9, Article 82. 11. Plotkin SA. This article reviews correlates of vaccine-induced immunity. Published in Clinical Infectious Diseases on August 1, 2008, Volume 47, Issue 3, pages 401-409. 12. Plotkin SA. This paper discusses correlates of protection induced by vaccination. Published in Clinical Vaccine Immunology in July 2010, Volume 17, Issue 7, pages 1055-1065. 13. U.S. Food and Drug Administration. This proposed rule outlines regulations for the accelerated approval of new drugs, antibiotics, and biological drug products. Published in the Federal Register in 1992, pages 13234-13235. 14. Tiernan R. This document provides a regulatory perspective on the development of preventive vaccines for global infectious diseases. 15. International Council for Harmonisation (ICH). The E8 guideline outlines general considerations for clinical trials. Published in 1997. 16. International Council for Harmonisation (ICH). The E9 guideline details statistical principles for clinical trials. Published in 1998. 17. Committee for Proprietary Medicinal Products, European Agency for the Evaluation of Medicinal Products. This guidance document addresses the clinical evaluation of new vaccines (CPMP/EWP/463/97). Published in London by the European Medicines Agency (EMEA) in 1999. 18. World Health Organization (WHO). Annex 1 of the WHO Technical Report Series No. 924 provides guidelines on the clinical evaluation of vaccines, including regulatory expectations. Published in 2004.
